## Purpose and entry points
This is the OPC Foundation’s cross-platform .NET 2.0 reference implementation of OPC UA. It ships composable NuGet libraries rather than one application: applications host servers or clients through DI/fluent builders, or run supplied samples/tools. The solution root is `UA.slnx`; representative runnable entry points are `samples/Reference/ConsoleReferenceServer/Program.cs`, `samples/Reference/ConsoleReferenceClient/Program.cs`, and the MCP executable `tools/Opc.Ua.Mcp/Program.cs`.

## Type system, encoding, and information models
`Opc.Ua.Types` is the foundational protocol model: built-in UA values, NodeIds, node tables/state objects, and binary/JSON/XML encoders. `Opc.Ua.Core.Types` adds common service contracts and canonical UA node states; `Opc.Ua.Core` supplies stack-level implementation and security. Model NodeSets are first-class inputs/assets and can be consumed at runtime or used for generated code.
- `src/Opc.Ua.Types/Encoders/BinaryEncoder.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Types/State/NodeState.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Core.Types/State/BaseEventState.cs`

## Transport and secure service pipeline
The core stack maps UA service requests through transport bindings, secure channels, endpoint dispatch, and server request queues. UA-TCP is implemented directly; HTTPS/WebSocket and Web API hosting integrate with ASP.NET Core/Kestrel. Transport abstractions isolate wire protocol implementations from client/session and server logic.
- `src/Opc.Ua.Core/Stack/Tcp/UaSCBinaryChannel.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Core/Stack/Server/EndpointBase.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Bindings.Https/Https/HttpsTransportListener.cs`

## Server runtime and address space
`Opc.Ua.Server` hosts `StandardServer`, sessions, subscriptions, diagnostics, security/role services, and pluggable NodeManagers. `MasterNodeManager` is the central boundary between OPC UA service dispatch and application address spaces; custom, fluent, generated, or runtime-NodeSet managers supply nodes, read/write behavior, methods, events, and monitoring. Historian providers and file-system services are optional server capabilities.
- `src/Opc.Ua.Server/Hosting/OpcUaServerHostedService.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Server/NodeManager/MasterNodeManager.ServiceDispatch.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Server/Server/StandardServer.cs`

## Client runtime
`Opc.Ua.Client` provides discovery, sessions, browse/read/write/call operations, node caching, subscriptions, alarms, history, and managed reconnect/failover. Managed sessions sit above channel management and session service clients; subscription engines convert Publish responses into monitored-item notifications and recovery state.
- `src/Opc.Ua.Client/Session/ManagedSession.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Client/Session/Subscription/DefaultSubscriptionEngine.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Core/Stack/Client/Channels/ClientChannelManager.cs`

## Security, identity, discovery, and resilience
Security spans X.509 certificate lifecycle/trust lists, cryptographic policy/provider selection, username/X.509/JWT-issued-token identities, and authorization. GDS/LDS packages provide certificate/application registration and local/global discovery. Redundancy packages add shared-state, Raft/lease leadership, peer discovery, replicated sessions/address space, and Kubernetes integration.
- `src/Opc.Ua.Core/Security/Certificates/CertificateManager/CertificateManager.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Gds.Server/ApplicationsNodeManager.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.Redundancy/Raft/DefaultRaftConsensus.cs`

## PubSub and external integrations
`Opc.Ua.PubSub` builds scheduled publisher/subscriber runtimes from validated configuration: data-set sources → writer groups → JSON/UADP encoding/security → transport; inbound frames reverse into reader groups and sinks. Transport packages support UDP/DTLS, Ethernet, MQTT, and Kafka. Companion-model libraries layer DI/client/server façades for Device Integration, ISA-95, robotics, vision, AI, OpenUSD, positioning, WoT Connectivity, and registries.
- `src/Opc.Ua.PubSub/Application/PubSubApplication.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.PubSub/Connections/PubSubConnection.cs`
- `src/Opc.Ua.PubSub/Transcoding/PubSubTranscodingBridge.cs`

## Build-time tooling and operations
Roslyn source generators turn model designs/NodeSets into types, NodeManagers, client/server APIs, and resource bindings; migration analyzers/code fixes support 1.x-to-2.0 adoption. The MCP host exposes controlled OPC UA client, PubSub, diagnostics, robotics, and vision operations to MCP-capable agents. CI runs Azure Pipelines and GitHub workflows; Docker/Kubernetes manifests are primarily for samples and integration deployment.
- `tools/Opc.Ua.SourceGeneration/ModelSourceGenerator.cs`
- `tools/Opc.Ua.MigrationAnalyzer/Analyzers/UA0001UtilsTraceToILoggerAnalyzer.cs`
- `tools/Opc.Ua.Mcp/McpHostBuilder.cs`
